Subject: Meridian on-prem: cluster footprint, storage separation, and QoS questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the intro yesterday. Meridian's platform team is kicking off a private deployment in our Broomfield colo and we need to map out cluster requirements and storage architecture before we lock the SOW. High level:

- Single region (Broomfield) with strict egress controls; no traffic to public internet except via a customer-managed NAT.
- We plan to run a production serving cluster (gpu-backed) + staging + a small dev cluster. Production will host inference-serving + KV cache + async ingestion workers.
- For production we expect peak 700 concurrent streams, avg seq len 512, and bursty spikes during daily batch windows.
- We prefer local NVMe for KV/cache but need long-term object/block for artifacts and logs.
- Questions: recommended node pool splits (GPU types, counts), QoS classes for serving vs preproc, eviction thresholds and persistent volume class mapping. Also curious about recommended PV bind policy for ephemeral workload (fast startup).

Can you share a short preflight checklist and a rough node-slice proposal so our infra team can validate? We can do a workshop next week.

--

Thanks team — quick architecture proposal below (will include diagrams in the workshop slide deck). Attaching the node-slice PDF with exact counts and PVC mapping.

Summary recommendations (production cluster):
- Node pools:
  - serving-gpu-pool (3 x 8xA100 nodes / autoscale to 6): dedicated, Guaranteed QoS; local NVMe for KV cache mounted as ephemeral (tmpfs for hot pages + KV store persistence to local NVMe).
  - preproc-cpu-pool (6 x 48vCPU/384GB): Burstable QoS; handles tokenization & batching; PVCs on blockstore-class (fast-ssd).
  - infra-pool (2 x 16vCPU): system services, router, logging agents; standard storage, lower IO SLA.

- Storage patterns:
  - NVMe-local (local-ssd-class): used for KV in-memory snapshots and model shard caches. Backups: periodic async rsync to blockstore / object-store.
  - blockstore-fastssd (WaitForFirstConsumer): model artifacts, checkpointing with 3d retention TTL in long-term object storage.
  - logs & metrics: shipped to customer-managed object store (S3-compatible) via agent; retention governed by Meridian policy.

- QoS / eviction thresholds:
  - Guaranteed for serving containers; eviction threshold set at 20% free disk on NVMe to avoid cold-start thrash.
  - Preemption policy: allow best-effort pods on preproc pool; set pod disruption budgets for serving replicas.

- PV binding + startup optimizations:
  - Use WaitForFirstConsumer for blockstore-fastssd to optimize topology-aware provisioning. For NVMe-local use local PersistentVolumes pre-provisioned per node with nodeAffinity.
  - LVM on NVMe for ephemeral scratch (logical volumes per pod) to avoid fragmentation at scale.

Known risks & asks for Meridian:
- Confirm whether local NVMe is single-disk per node or RAIDed; affects eviction and backup cadence.
- Confirm allowed egress endpoints (we recommend a small allowlist for telemetry + artifact sync).

Attachments: proposed-node-slices.pdf (detailed counts and PVC templates)

I'll add concrete kubernetes YAML snippets and IO numbers to the deck for the workshop.

—Monica
